# Mahjong: Soar agent from the Rosie teaching script

**Runnable.** `mahjong.soar` loads the shared library (`Soar/soar-library`, v2.42) and `mahjong-rules.soar` (17 task rules, generated by `gen.py` from the statements in `english-input.txt`; `tools/rosie_solitaire.py`). Generated 18 Nov 2026. Needs Soar 9.6.6 (or the PyPI soar-sml bindings).

## Run

    python3 ../../tools/run_agent.py . mahjong.soar --seed 1 --cap 60000
    python3 ../../tools/run_agent.py . mahjong.soar --json | python3 ../../tools/check_moves.py mahjong init-mahjong.world

`python3 gen.py WORLD` writes the same rules with another example state as the initial world.

## Results (library v2.42, 18 Nov 2026)

Example states (`gen.py WORLD`, `run_agent.py --check`): init-mahjong: goal false, failure false; final-mahjong: goal true, failure false.

Seeds 1-3, cap 60,000 decisions; plans replayed independently by `check_moves.py` (legality from the action statements, the losing conditions, the goal).

| Seed | Outcome | Decisions | Actions | Replay |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | success | 1,134 | 4 | goal holds |
| 2 | success | 1,161 | 4 | goal holds |
| 3 | success | 1,224 | 4 | goal holds |

## Translation

- Operator move-pair (argument1, argument2 = the two blocks), statement 4: two different clear available blocks of the same
  colour go onto the garbage location. available (not on a location, statement 5) and clear (statement 6) are maintained
  one-argument relations; a block that a moved block was on becomes clear.
- The goal (statement 8) is expanded over the blocks of the world file: every block is on the garbage.
Propose initialize-mahjong when its conditions below hold.

The assumption codes (A-S, A-G, A-C, A-P) are explained in `tools/rosie_solitaire.py` and `../../PILOT.md`.
